column3: RANDALL: I'm sure, whenever I'm meant to go home, that key will find its way to me somehow.
In fact, that's why I picked up ol' Klefki here!
Little feller's like a magnet for lost keys, so every now and then I check if he picked it up.
No dice so far, but I'm figurin' it's only a matter of time.
By the ways, I don't suppose you's thinkin' something like...

Wait a second, weren't he just in that Night Club?
map_0595#6		Surely you ain't in two places at once!
And you'd be right as rain, I ain't.
No one's gonna be spendin' their whole day behind a counter, you know?
I been back-and-forthin' it between here and there to keep up on my reading.
If it seems like I'm in two places at once, it's prolly just a coink-a-dink.
RANDALL: Hey, if it ain't--
Well, whatever your name were.
Good to see ya made it out of Gehovasect witness' place or what you ever had that was.
I sallied on outta there a bit ago... Fell back into some bad habitats...
But now here I am again, and doing better than ever!
This shelter openin' up is a blessing better than their Arceus whatnot could ever hope to give.
The staff are real friendly and all, and look at all the books they helped me collect!
To tell the truth, I've still got a lot more books back home, but variety is the spicy life, right?
Still, it'd be nice to be able to go home someday.
I live here in ol' Reborn, of course.
The only problem is...
I done lost my key to my house.
So I tried to call the locksmith, right? But any ID I got was in there, and the property ain't even in my name--
So they just assumed I was bamboozlin' them to break into some poor fellow's homestead.
I could break a window or somethin' somethin'...
But at that point I decided, fate don't want me to be at home right then.
So I adopted vagrancy and whimsituditnousness into my daily life!
It's been quite an experience, even if I am feelin' the tail end of it.
I'm sure, whenever I'm meant to go home, that key will find its way to me somehow.
Ah, say there, that wouldn't happen to be my key that you's holdin' on to?
\PN handed over the 'R' Key.
Well, I'll be damned. You're a better Klefki than Klefki is.
Guess that means I can go home at any time.
Well, I've still got a lot I'd like to finish reading here, so I'll mosey on home whenever I wrap up.
Can't help but think that might be a mite borin' for Klefki if I won't be travellin' around now though...
I think you'll get more use out of 'er than I will now.
Why don't you take care of 'er?
It's been real, partner.
RANDALL: I've still got a lot I'd like to finish reading here, so I'll mosey on home whenever I wrap up.
Ugh, trying to do homework in a place like this is infuriating!
I can't go three minutes without a random stranger bothering me!
Yes, that means you!
Blankets, pillows, towels, rations here.
If you're missing anything, please don't hesitate to ask!
Our supplies are low, but we will do our best to provide for you as well as we can!
Hey, keep it on the DL from staff... but I'm packin' candy if you need a level up.
\PN obtained PULSE Read-Out 04!
PULSE Dex updated!
Sigh... If we're at this capacity, I don't know how much longer our food donations will last.
Hopefully the citizens will contribute more, or that we'll be able to get a supply train going soon.
ARC: Okay, with you all out, I think everyone is all safe and accounted for.
CAIN: We did a last comb through the place to check too-- seems like all the civilians are right as the sprinkler-set rain.
LANA: Aya, we were SO worried about you!
In a place like that-- a girl like you--
Even I was scared!
TEZ: I coulda taken them.
But I'm told you handled it all by yourself.
Not bad, for a girl.
LANA: And you made it unscathed! That's our little Gym Leader rockstar!
AYA: Okay, mom, seriously--
LANA: And you managed to defend your delinquent friends. A noble heart indeed!
AYA: SERIOUSLY.
Can you stop talking and listen to me for once?
Maybe now of all times, while you're heaping praise on me?
Instead of rattling on about how proud you are about me, would you actually stop for a second and listen to what I have to say?
LANA: Of-- of course, dear...
AYA: Because you have that problem a lot.
You're always going on about being a good mother, but when it comes time to listen and offer genuine support, you're clueless.
Case in point, you have an entire other child you're STILL neglecting.
You don't have to see eye to eye with his decisions, but you do have to shut up about it and be there for him.
At LEAST enough so that he doesn't feel safer on the literal streets rather than being around you.
LANA: I'm-- sorry, I'm just... not terribly comfortable with the whole 'gay' thing...
CAIN: I'm not even gay.
For some reason everyone thinks I am,
But one of the first things I ever said to \PN was that she's cute!
Girls or guys or whatever--
But girls or guys or whatever--
I've got a lot of mixed feelings about it all still, but I don't see why anyone should like just one category of people.
AYA: You haven't even taken the time to understand that much about your own child.
I'm still mad at you, by the way.
CAIN: That's fine.
I'd probably be mad at me too in your position.
LANA: Well, I...
AYA: No, just don't.
You don't need to argue; don't defend yourself.
Just think about it, maybe?
TEZ: You can't tell her not to defend herself.
You're not the parent here.
You may've saved the day, allegedly, but that doesn't give you the right to talk to her like that.
AYA: You're right; it doesn't give me that right.
I always had it.
I'm only just now using it because I just fought like fifty armored Legendaries and my entire bloodstream has been replaced by adrenaline.
And frankly, they're a lot scarier than you'll ever be, so let's double down.
Everything you say is rude and awful and I hate you.
At your best you're chauvinistic and at your worst you're abusive-- not just to me, but Mom too.
LANA: H-honey, that's just--
AYA: No, don't make excuses for him.
He needs to take accountability for his behavior, or he needs to go.
Maybe both.
TEZ: You NEED to learn some goddamn respect.
I'll make you regret ever speaking to me like--
TITANIA: I don't think so.
TEZ: What the hell is your problem?
Don't do anything you'll regret now...
TITANIA: I'm not the one who will regret it.
Apparently you already forgot our little chat earlier, so this is a reminder.
Anything you do to her, you'll get tenfold from me.
HARDY: Make that double on my count too.
TEZ: Tch... You can't really expect to get away with threats like this.
ARC: Funny you say that.
Every other thing I've heard you say has been half a threat.
If you don't like the music, best you change your tune.
TEZ: The authorities are gonna hear about this...
CAIN: You're still doing it.
TITANIA: Threats are the only way some men know how to communicate.
Running to their betters is just the last resort form of it.
ARC: You do know that all of us work in tandem with the police and city authorities, right?
Don't suppose you picked up on that among the whole escorting civilians out of here thing?
AYA: That's enough.
Mom, get him out of here.
Take him or whatever.
Consider finding another set of divorce papers on your way.
LANA: I...
...Let's... Let's just go, dear.
TEZ: Hmph.
HARDY: Yo, that was... intense.
AYA: Thanks for the backup.
Frankly I'm glad I had it there rather than with the Genesect.
They may be scarier than him, but they're not waiting for me at home.
...I hope.
CAIN: Making it day by day with the help of your friends isn't so bad~
AYA: I bet.
Starting to think you had the right idea.
HARDY: I guess I really don't gotta look out for you so much anymore, huh.
AYA: Only thanks to your help in the first place.
AYA: Yours as well, Titania.
Even if you can be a bit harsh...
It helped. Thanks.
TITANIA: Glad to hear it.
You did well.
AYA: You're cool too.
ARC: Word.
AYA: And thanks, \PN, for being the one actually there for it all.
AYA: ...Well, should we get back to rehearsal?
TITANIA: Are you sure you're even up to that after everything?
AYA: Psh.
After all that?
Sure.
I can get up in front of a crowd and fuck a few notes up.
Whatever, not like they're gonna ruin my home life or bring in the nightmare factory.
CAIN: That's the... spirit?
I think?
ARC: Think it might be best to rain check this one.
I'm beat.
Can't imagine you're not either.
HARDY: We can pick it up again later.
You and I can get an extra practice sesh in before then.
And next time, we'll tear it up even better!
AYA: Works for me.
ARC: All right, then that's a one, two, and break.
We'll see you all next time!
LIN: hey
why don't you come step into my office for a sec
Excuse me, my dear. Wouldst thou like to accompany me on a most exquisite outing?
Tch, this isn't working at all.
I'm trying to learn to be a Casanova, but this whole romantic thing is harder than it looks.
Maybe I just need to wear green...
Greetings, my beautiful blossom.
I've been waiting for you,
Though I never knew it until now.
A single glimpse into your eyes has shown me a future I was blind to, and now that I have seen it, I shall look at no other.

To tell you the truth, doc, the plants were terrifying.
But I was always more afraid of the people.
Did you know?
The best place to train your Attack stat is in a hidden playground in the slums!
The best place to train your Attack stat is around the area where the slums used to be!
So, I understand that you've had some anxiety around this area after the attacks a bit ago.
Could you tell me about that?
Would you like to purchase a ticket? \ch[321,-1,Grandview Station,Goldenrod Station,Ivyline Station,Sunset Station,Peony Station,Kingsbury Station,Shantyport Station]
Excuse me, I'm a bit busy right now.
I'm making preparations for this place to become a station for the rebuilt railnet system.
We've also got people working just on the other side of Beryl Wall to run the tracks from Grandview Station up under the Jasper and Beryl Wards.
Of course, it's still going to take a lot more time and money for this project to be completed, so please be patient!
EVE: This is the girl you told me about?
LASS: Oh, hi!
Are you the nurse?
EVE: I'm the doctor.
LASS: Oh!
...At your age?
EVE: It's in progress.
But if you really want your problem fixed, I'm the best person for the job.
The clinic knows that too.
Now, how can I help you?
LASS: Er, so...
To get right to it, back when the lake was still pretty filthy, my Ducklett ran into it,
And when I tried to rescue him, I ended up falling in too.
Just for a second! But I swallowed some of the murk, and,
Well, I've had a recurring cough since.
It comes and goes, but...
My friends finally convinced me to see someone about it.
Do you know how hard it is to find a good Doctor in this region?
And especially with the insurance situation!
There was one guy who was offering off-market pharmaceuticals, but apparently he's gone now.
And every other search just turns up some old psychiatrist who went missing.
Anyway, I've been concerned, because my Ducklett--
Huh???
LASS: Hey, get-- come here!
EVE: ...
LASS: Just, sometimes he sounds a little hoarse too.
DUCKLETT: Ducc.
EVE: Well, I'm sure we can do something.
I'll have you both follow me upstairs.
Say, how does your Ducklett feel about Shaymin?
LASS: Shaymin?!
You have one here?
EVE: No,
Not just one.

Uggggh, I totally just got suspended from the Onyx Trainers' School!
This SUCKS!
Just because I went on a huge losing streak, they're giving me a time out? How is that supposed to help?!
But noooo, they just shove me off with some crumpled notice in my hands and telling me how to recover from a period of weakness--
Like, who cares?!
I don't even wanna look at this right now. You take it!
I should just transfer to Apophyll.
I bet they'd be more forgiving AND have fewer stupid policies!

Hello, Trainer. Challenging the Gym League, are you?
You know, our daughter is a Gym Leader!
Actually, she's lots of things!
Computer technician, lion tamer at Agate Circus!
We are SO proud of her.
She's a real peach; I'm sure you'd absolutely love her!
You know, for a while, we were really worried about our little girl.
She always locked herself away in her room, and she was so shy she wouldn't talk to anyone!
She wasn't the type to make friends at school, but she never went anywhere else, so she just played video games all day.
What kind of future can someone like that have, we thought?
Then one day, just all of a sudden, she told us she was going off to pursue her life's secret dream of joining the circus.
And she did great!
Maybe sometimes you just gotta let kids do their thing until they're ready.
Everything that happened to our girl is a little hard to believe...
But if it is true, then we owe you big time.
Thanks for bringing her back.
We've been so lonely after our daughter took off to go earn her place in the world.
It's normal for parents after the kid leaves the nest, I think.
Of course, I'm happy she's off living her life.
It's just...
She changed so drastically in a short period of time.
I would be lying if I said I hadn't thought drugs were involved, but she always came up totally clean.
Strange, children can be.
Maybe our daughter changed as a result of meeting that girl...
The timing makes sense, but how could a kid like that have such an impact on her?
I would say one never knows what might become a formative experience, but...
It doesn't quite add up, you know?
If she went into social work, for instance, after we tried to adopt that orphan girl, it would make sense.
But the Circus? Where did that come from!?
It's almost like she became a completely different person overnight.
Ah well, as long as she's happy.
Ah...
If our daughter joins a terrorist organization and then gets deleted and recovered from a fantasy space void by the powers of God...
Uh, does that make us bad parents?
Guests and registered visitors only beyond the lobby, please.

TERRA: Mom, Dad, you here?
MOM: Honey, how've you been?!
It's so nice to see you!
How long has it been?
We've seen you on the posters, and you know we are SO proud.
I love the hair, but I can see those roots!
DAD: To what do we owe the pleasure all of the sudden?
TERRA: I brought a friend.
This is \PN. He's the champion.
This is \PN. She's the champion.
This is \PN. They're the champion.
DAD: Well, well, well...
Nice to meet you, Champion.
Thanks for being a friend to our daughter.
Just a peach, isn't she?
TERRA: Stop it, Dad.
Actually, there's something I should tell you guys...
I brought \PN because I thought it might help to have someone else who was involved, and who's trustworthy.
But I got mixed up in something I shouldn't have, and I did some... less than great things.
DAD: Oh, come on, the circus isn't that bad.
MOM: Not now, darling...
DAD: Right, right... Sorry, go on?
TERRA: Before I left, I was bored.
Actually, maybe more like depressed.
MOM: Depressed?
I mean-- honey, that's serious...
Did we... do something?
TERRA: Probably not.
I don't know what could have been done.
I just realized how inconsequential everything was.
A normal family with a normal life and perfectly reasonable parents...
To a lot of people, I'm sure that's way more than they ever had, and I'm just selfish and spoiled.
But then, at least they had a reason for their problems.
Stories are full of heroes and characters with zany powers, and this was just...
School.
Home.
Sleep.
Just like however many billion other people.
I wanted to do something different.
MOM: Sure, I don't see the problem...
DAD: And that's why you left.
Do you still feel that way now?
TERRA: No.
Not at all.
DAD: Then I'd say the lion-taming was worth it!
TERRA: ...This isn't about the circus, Dad.
I got over it, and I'm still having lots of fun with the people I've met.
I'm lucky to have people like \PN who appreciate me.
I'm lucky to have people like \PN who tolerate me.
But there's a lot of guilt that I have to take responsibility for and still find a way to move forward with.
MOM: I don't understand what you mean.
TERRA: ...So, do you guys remember that girl that stayed with us for a bit?
MOM: Of course!
Quite a character she was!
TERRA: Yeah, so, turns out she actually kind of became god for a while.
DAD: ...She what?

We've already introduced a couple new species to this area, but to make sure each new one gets along, we keep close watch over them here.
Ah! I've heard about you!
You're that Trainer who provided the rest of the funding we needed to rebuild this place.
Truly, young Trainer, you have my sincerest gratitude.
Repopulating the region, starting with just this island, has been a dream of mine ever since Reborn fell into decline.
Thank you so much for making this possible once again. I will not forget your kindness.
Welcome, Trainer. This here is the newly reopened Azurine Nature Center.
We're working with our sister facility up in Aventurine to make sure all kinds of species have a safe home in Reborn.
We're currently repopulating this island with certain species. If you find them out in the wild, you're free to catch them, but please take only what you need.
There was a bunch of junk left over here from when we tore up the old building.
Most of it was useless, but some of it's still laying around.
If there's anything here you can use, feel free to take it.
Let's see... Next we should introduce...
Shroomish, maybe?
It would be most appropriate for this sort of habitat.
Of course, that may not happen any time soon at the rate the Bulbasaur project is going.
Hello there, \PN!
I received word from the Grand Hall that you might be coming by to assist with our restoration program!
Thank you so much for being able and generous enough to offer your time to the Azurine Center on top of your already valuable time!
In the near future, we're primarily looking to introduce two species to the Azurine ecosystem:
Pansage and Fomantis.
In order to do this, we'll need a pair of mature Lurantis, one male and one female, and a pair of adult Simisage, again, one male and female each.
